items.component: MegaMoE NVFP4 W4A4 (dispatch+fc1+act+fc2+combine incl. P11/P12 NVLink), 92 layers
items.basis: UNMEASURED-new-kernel in-step (bounded range 244-304 ms). Model: optables nvfp4 MOE.dispatch/fc1/act/fc2/combine 96.48 ms + comm_ach P11 22.48 + P12 78.96 = 197.9 ms. In the model the layer is link-bound: link 2.139 ms/layer vs GEMM ops 1.049 ms/layer. LOW = MEASURED standalone FlashInfer 6e438852b nvfp4w_nvfp4a EP16 T=16384: 2649.3 us/layer x 92 = 243.7 ms (moe/rows.json, moe/README; derate 1.231, matches calibrated.json megamoe.nvfp4w_nvfp4a['16'] T16384). HIGH/central = vendored megamoe_rubin in-step, inferred: the mxfp4 F8K MegaMoE excl is 207.31 ms (prefill rows MOE.megamoe). Scaling x1.92-2.03 (FI MX T8192 1690-1789 to T16384 3427 us) gives MX F16K 397-421 ms. The release NVFP4-act arm saves 116.5 ms (P3-16 F16K 1179.8 to 1063.3 ms, prefill rows 'full step'), so NV vendored is about 281-304 ms (central 292).
items.root_cause: (a) In-tree kernel is the older vendored megamoe_rubin. It runs separate staging kernels: router_kernel 31.21 ms and reduce_bf16 6.82 ms busy per step at F8K, versus 0.5% staging in FI (moe README). It is 1.2x FI at EP16 (1096 vs 901 us at T4096). (b) Even FI hides only part of the GEMMs under the link. Link bytes are 0.4955 GB FP4 dispatch + 1.762 GB BF16 combine per layer. At the measured practical 1.144 TB/s that is a 1.973 ms floor, but the layer takes 2.649 ms, so about 0.68 ms/layer of the 1.05 ms of GEMM work stays exposed. (c) A single 16K call is slower than two 8K calls: NV T8192 is 1254.2 us, so 2x8K = 2508 us vs 2649 us at 16K.
items.fix: 1) Wire FI 6e438852b NVFP4 MegaMoE into specialized_prefill for P3-16. Use per-shape dispatch with 8,192-token sub-calls at T=16K (2508 vs 2649 us/layer), and absorb routing staging into the kernel. 2) Kernel: finer-grained phase interleave. Push combine rows per fc2 output tile as soon as the tile retires, and run the next expert's dispatch receives under the current fc1, so that layer time approaches max(link 1.97, ops 1.05) + one-expert drain. Combine stays BF16 and dispatch stays FP4 (official rules); no dedup, which C7 measured as 1.4-3.8% slower.

items.component: KDA chain: core_prefill (FlashKDA recurrence + prepare) + conv + gated o_norm, 69 layers
items.basis: MEASURED mxfp4 (kernel unchanged under nvfp4; FP32 state). Model: core 11.52 + conv 3.80 + o_norm 0.84 ms. core_prefill: the model's serial floor does not scale with F (11.49 ms at both F8K and F16K, model_tables.json), so a ratio transfer is invalid. I used ops1 kda-077 at the F16K shape (3 seq x 96 heads, fp32): 699.4 us x 69 = 48.3 ms. In-step F8K was 27.67 ms (recurrence 15.40 + prepare 11.17 + gather 0.57), and x2 gives 55.3; range 48.3-55.3, central 51.8. conv: derate 4.29 (k3conv::qkv_conv_kernel 8.16 ms at F8K) gives 16.3 ms. o_norm: derate 12.24 (_kda_rmsnorm_gated 5.17 ms at F8K) gives 10.3 ms.
items.root_cause: 96 heads at TP1 fall off the v-split FlashKDA build onto the stock path. That gives only nseq x heads = 288 CTAs, each doing a chunk-serial walk over 5.4K tokens. _flash_kda_fwd_prepare is a separate full pass (40% of in-step core time). conv and gated RMSNorm are standalone HBM passes over q/k/v and o, which the model assumes are fused.
items.fix: (1) Build or instantiate the v-split FlashKDA variant for 96 heads x fp32 state so the P3-16 shape gets 2-4x more CTAs. (2) Fuse prepare into the recurrence prologue. items.component: DSA sparse MLA + prologue (fp8 q quant, head pad, KV insert) + gate_mul, 24 layers
items.basis: MEASURED mxfp4 (kernel unchanged). sparse_mla derate 3.295 (fmhaSm107a...HQk576HV512HVPerCta256 24.74 ms + index_remap 0.69 ms at F8K), giving 15.43 to 50.9 ms; ops1 sparse_mla-161 at F16K standalone gives 2480 us x 24 = 59.5. prologue+aux at F8K was 6.55 ms (scaled_fp8_quant_kernel_strided_group_shape 2.60, _pad_query_heads_kernel 2.06, concat_and_cache_mla 0.84), x2 = 13.1. gate_mul (gate_sigmoid_mul_kernel) 1.69 x2 = 3.4.
items.root_cause: The trtllm-gen kernel is the decode formulation. It pads 96 to 128 heads (1.33x). HVPerCta256 splits V512 so each CTA recomputes the 576-wide QK^T per V half. Each Q64 tile re-gathers its own 2048 KV rows. It runs at about 3.4-3.8 PF padded vs the FP8 MMA rate, and is not HBM-bound (cold equals warm, ops1). The prologue runs as separate quant, pad and insert kernels that the model treats as fused.
items.fix: A prefill-form CuTe sparse-MLA for sm107 in kimi_k3: native 96 heads (no pad, which also removes _pad_query_heads), one QK^T per tile feeding both 256-wide PV halves from TMEM, and a double-buffered paged-KV gather. Exact top-k indices; FP8 KV as stored. Fuse fp8 q-quant into the qb_wq_packed GEMM epilogue, and the sigmoid gate_mul into the sparse-MLA epilogue or the o_proj prologue.
items.expected_gain_pct_step: -30 to -40 ms (-3.5 to -4.7%): sparse_mla to ~1.5x model (~23 ms), prologue and gate_mul to ~2 ms
items.effort: L: new attention kernel (the decode kernel cannot be retuned into it)
items.dependencies: Shared with the decode sparse-MLA work only loosely (different formulation)
items.confidence: high on excess; medium on attainable ratio
items.verify_with: ops1 sparse_mla-161 (16384 rows, 96 heads, 2048 keys, kv_row 576 B, fp8, pool 235K rows), target <=1.0 ms/layer, plus an ncu tensor-pipe % check. Then the DSA block in the P3-16 step profile.

items.component: DSA indexer: idx_score (deep_gemm sm100_mqa_logits) + exact top-k (trtllm GVR) + idx q-quant/insert, 24 layers
items.basis: MEASURED mxfp4 (unchanged; MXFP4 indexer KV in both checkpoints). idx_score derate 1.427 (20.65 ms at F8K) gives 41.3 ms. topk derate 3.875 (GvrMainKernel 8.74 ms at F8K) gives 17.5. idx_q_quant+insert 1.34 ms x2 = 2.7. Cross-check ops1 dsa_indexer_topk-080 at F16K: logits 1478 + topk 1086 us per layer (derate 1.84).
items.root_cause: Top-k is a decode-oriented per-row top-2048 over ~78K FP32 logits with multi-pass sampling. It re-reads a 16384 x 78K logits scratch that the model prices as one write plus one read. The logits kernel is the sm100 deep_gemm on sm107 at 1.43x the FP4 rate. The q quant and the cp_gather/insert are separate kernels.
items.fix: An exact two-stage prefill top-k. First, fuse a per-row radix histogram into the mqa_logits epilogue, so the threshold bucket is known at tile write. Second, run a single select pass over only the candidate bucket. This stays exact: ties and threshold are resolved exactly, with a graph-safe exact fallback if the bucket overflows. Also fuse the MXFP4 q quant into the q-projection epilogue.
items.dependencies: none
items.verify_with: ops1 dsa_indexer_topk-080 shape (16384 rows, 75.6K mean keys, top 2048, mxfp4 keys), target logits+topk <=1.6 ms/layer, plus a bit-exact index-set check vs the current GVR.

items.component: MoE router path: router BF16 GEMM + router top-k + latent_down/up BF16 GEMMs + latent RMSNorm, 92 layers
items.basis: MEASURED mxfp4 (unchanged, BF16). router derate 1.568 gives 8.3 ms. router_topk_kernel 3.38 ms at F8K, x2 = 6.8 (model 0.06). latent_down 1.184 gives 25.1, latent_up 1.173 gives 24.9. latent_norm rms_norm_rows_kernel 1.62 x2 = 3.2.

items.component: Shared experts MXFP8 (gate_up + SiLU-mul + down) and side-stream overlap with MegaMoE, 92 layers
items.basis: UNMEASURED-new-kernel for the GEMMs (MXFP8 replaces BF16). Bounded range 52.2-61.6 ms, central 56.4: gate_up 24.75-32.7 (low = 24.36 x in-step BF16 derate 1.016; high = ops1 gemm-091 scaled_mm 314.2 + act-quant 41.1 us, x92); down 13.76-16.2 (low x1.13; high = gemm-076 142.2 + 34.4 us, x92). shared_act is MEASURED and unchanged: situ_and_mul_vec8 6.34 ms at F8K, x2 = 12.7 ms (model 0.84). Overlap MEASURED at F8K (prefill/analysis/p3g.attr.txt): MoE block busy 340.15 vs excl 308.90 ms, so only 31.25 ms of kernel time overlaps, about the size of the vendored staging router_kernel (31.21 ms). shared_experts excl is 63.86 ms, i.e. the side stream hides essentially none of the shared GEMMs under the persistent MegaMoE.
items.root_cause: The persistent MegaMoE grid occupies all SMs, so the side-stream shared GEMMs serialize. SiLU-mul is a separate kernel. Under MXFP8, each GEMM also needs a separate activation-quant kernel (34-63 us each, ops1 notes). The model itself charges shared serially, so it gives no credit for overlap.
items.fix: Under nvfp4 the MegaMoE layer is NVLink-bound (link 2.14 ms vs GEMMs 1.05 ms per layer in the model), so tensor cores sit about 50% idle. Launch MegaMoE with a per-shape SM budget (persistent grid N-k SMs) and run the shared MXFP8 gate_up(+fused SiLU-mul + MXFP8 quant epilogue) -> down chain concurrently on the k reserved SMs, sized so it finishes inside the MegaMoE time. Fuse the MXFP8 activation quant for shared_gate_up into the AttnRes-post output.
items.expected_gain_pct_step: Excess removal -15 to -20 ms, plus overlap hiding most of the remaining ~37-40 ms, which goes below the model's 532.9. Total -40 to -57 ms (-5 to -7%). The model should add max(MegaMoE, shared on k SMs).

items.dependencies: FI MegaMoE wiring (item 1). Measure MegaMoE slowdown at N-k SMs.

- mxfp4 824.7 ms: MoE 393.0 (47.7%: experts 169.5, shared 110.0, comm 65.6); DSA 105.6 (12.8%); KDA 293.2 (35.6%: kda_proj 275.8 BF16); rest 32.8 (4.0%).
- So nvfp4 removes 291.8 ms, all of it from GEMMs: kda_proj -182, experts -73, shared -73. Exposed link time rises +35.9 ms because MegaMoE becomes NVLink-bound (link 2.14 vs ops 1.05 ms/layer). DSA and the small ops are untouched, so their share grows.
- At the projected step (central 847 ms): MoE 416.8 (49%), DSA 191.7 (23%), KDA 192.3 (23%), rest 46.1 (5%).

PROJECTED STEP (unbiased component sum): central 846.6 ms, range 774.7-886.8 = 348.9 unchanged-kernel components + KDA core 51.8 + MXFP8 KDA proj 109.7 + MXFP8 shared GEMMs 43.7 + MegaMoE 292 + 0.5 misc.
- Method check: the same transfer applied to mxfp4 F16K gives 1200-1223 vs measured 1179.8 (prefill rows full step). So F8K-derived derates over-project F16K by about 2-4%. Bias-corrected: about 825 ms (755-865), i.e. about 19.9K tok/s/GPU (18.9-21.7K) vs model 30.75K. That is a derate of about 1.55 vs model achievable.
- This is lower than calibrated.json prefill.nvfp4_modelopt P3-16 (22.77K, 719.4 ms). That number applies the whole-step ratio 1.35 from the release NVFP4-act arm. The ~190-200 ms of excess sitting in unchanged DSA/KDA/small-op kernels is additive, not proportional, so it does not shrink when the GEMMs get 2-3x faster. Recommend calibrate.py transfer per component (additive for unchanged kernels) rather than per step.

MODEL-VERSION CAVEAT: the prefill lane's derates (RESULTS.md: P3-16 1.23, MegaMoE 1.28) were computed against an older model that summed MegaMoE ops + P11 + P12 serially (model_tables.json P3-16 F16K t_ach 960.4). The current optables uses max(ops, link) + drain (824.7 for mxfp4). Against the current model, measured mxfp4 P3-16 F16K is 1.431 (calibrated.json prefill P3-16), and in-step vendored MegaMoE is about 1.69-1.79x. Non-MoE per-op t_ach values are identical in both models, so those per-op derates transfer as-is.

BEST CHUNK: the model's best is F=64K, but only +0.3% (30.84K vs 30.75K tok/s/GPU, out/prefill.json nvfp4_modelopt|achievable|base P3-16 grid; t 2125 ms). Family shares are unchanged at 64K (MoE 53.3%, comm 404.9 of 2125 ms), and the O1 gain is +23.5% at 64K vs +20.2% at 16K. Measured F8K to F16K gained +3.6% tok/s (13.41K to 13.89K). Most excess items scale per token: sparse MLA, top-k, conv, norms, MegaMoE (FI favours 8K sub-calls). The only component expected to improve with larger F is the KDA recurrence, since more sequences per chunk means more CTAs. F64K is not bench-feasible at TP1 memory (need 239 GB in the model; F16K already needed a pinned KV pool). Conclusion: no chunk lever; keep F16K, with 2x8K sub-structure for MegaMoE/O1.

- **r8 projected: 17.7-19.6 ms, central 18.5 ms**, i.e. 1257-1391 tok/s/GPU, central about 1330. That is 1.16-1.20x over measured mxfp4.
- **r24 projected: 26.8-27.9 ms**, i.e. 2650-2760 tok/s/GPU.
- The per-family ledger built bottom-up from gap512 sums to 19.0-21.0 ms at r8 and about 28-29 ms at r24, about 5% above the anchor. That is the L190K / EP16 bias.
- **calibrated.json is optimistic.** Its d_rest is a ratio over achievable, so it scales the halved MXFP8 GEMM achievable by the BF16 derate. It also assumes the vendored x1.2 MoE factor.

**What changes kernel under nvfp4.** Only three components change, so their mxfp4 derates do not transfer:
- routed experts (NVFP4 W4A4 MegaMoE EP32)
- shared experts (BF16 to MXFP8)
- KDA in_proj / o_proj (BF16 to MXFP8)

Everything else stays BF16 or keeps its KV precision, so its gap512 in-step derate transfers directly: MLA/DSA projections, router, latent, f_b_proj, dense L0, drafter, lm_head, FP8 MLA KV, MXFP4 indexer, FP32 KDA state.

**Ranked excess.**
- At r8: MegaMoE 2.30 > shared MXFP8 1.02-1.48 > small unfused 1.47 > DCP top-k 1.31 > BF16 SP GEMMs 1.18 > DSA attention path 1.16 > KDA projection MXFP8 0.66-1.0 > KDA core 0.87 > drafter 0.28 > SP comm 0.16.
- At r24 the order shifts toward per-row terms: MegaMoE 2.67, DSA attention path 2.21, top-k 2.15, BF16 GEMMs 2.06 (g_proj SplitKGemm collapse), shared 1.4-2.0, KDA core 1.69 (2.26 at r32), small ops 1.47, KDA projection 0.9-1.4, drafter 0.96, SP comm 0.61.
- If all ten fixes reach their targets, r8 goes from about 18.5 ms to about 10 ms, i.e. about 2.4K tok/s/GPU, about 1.16x model ach.

**Suggested order.**
1. Wire FI EP32 NVFP4 MegaMoE into sdec and measure it in-step. This is a dependency for everything else.
2. Build the CuTe low-latency GEMM family: BF16 SP shapes plus MXFP8 with producer-fused quant. It covers four ledger rows, about 3.5 ms at r8 and about 5 ms at r24.
3. Exact single-pass DCP top-k.
4. Small-op fusions.
5. KDA core re-tile, which matters most at r24-32.
6. Sparse MLA with the 4 verify rows processed together, plus the fused MlaQuery.

**KV capacity and memory.**
- Model r_max for D3-32 nvfp4 is SOL 71.13 and achievable 68.67 (mxfp4: 64.89 / 62.64). Per request this is 2.65 GB; resident weights are 86.8 GB/GPU for nvfp4 vs 103.4 GB for mxfp4 (kv.capacity).
- Calibrated r_max is 44.8. That is the measured mxfp4 value: 2329 blocks, 138.0 GiB at gpu-memory-utilization 0.93, 13 blocks per request per DP rank (wave2/README.md, calibrated.json measured_rmax 'D3-32|k3').
- Projected nvfp4 r_max is about 49.8, because 16.5 GB of weights are freed per GPU.
- **The limit that binds is the code, not memory.** The SP path refuses more than 512 verify rows, which means r ≤ 32 (specialized_decode/runtime/__init__.py:53, specialized_decode_config).
- **So memory work does not matter for r ≤ 32.** It only becomes relevant if the 512-row cap is lifted to reach r of about 45-48.
  - The model gives r48 nvfp4 achievable 17.34 ms / 8527 tok/s/GPU, against 7269 at r32 (+17%).
  - At that point the fixed per-request block floor and the graph-capture memory would start to bind. The capture memory is the r32 bench OOM at 245 GiB, which needs a production check.

**Caveats.**
- All derates come from the release tree rel-1767cf7, dummy weights and balanced routing. The decode step benches have no numeric check.
- gap512 B92 ran with contexts scaled to 0.686x (mean 130K). B80 ran at L190K.
- The MegaMoE projection assumes in-step time equals standalone time. That held for the vendored kernel, 109 vs 109 us per layer.

result.overall:
Most of the ledger's numbers re-derive correctly from the cited files:

- gap512 B32/B92 exposed values and the derate transfers for BF16, DSA, top-k, KDA core, TAIL and SP comm

The central r8 projection (about 18.5 ms) survives, but for different reasons than stated.

Material errors:
1. Shared experts run at SP M=32 (r8) and M=96 (r24), not 128/384. This overstates the r24 shared term by about 0.5-0.6 ms.
2. Standalone cold timings are used as in-step without the about 0.88x factor seen on BF16.

result.overall:
The ledger is mostly accurate on code-level blockers. I re-read and confirmed the following:
- model.py:816 hard-codes MEGA_MOE_MXFP4.
- The expert mapping at model.py:585-602 covers only weight_packed and weight_scale. A '.weight_scale_2' name substring-matches and is rewritten to a param that does not exist.
- Rubin MegaMoE refuses non-MXFP4 formats (experts.py:289) and rejects weight_scale_2 / input_scale (experts.py:442).
- DeepGEMM MEGA_MOE_NVFP4 supports SwiGLU only (deep_gemm_mega_moe.py:164-172).
- The knob table covers only world sizes 4/8/16 (62 entries).
- sdec bf16_weight raises on quantized linears.
- The ModelOpt mixed get_quant_method behaves as described.
- The MXFP8 fast paths key on Mxfp8OnlineLinearMethod.

The cited microbench and model numbers also re-derive correctly (prefill/rows.json, ops1 gemm ids, moe_ep32 derates, wave2 decode table, optables totals).

The weak part is the projections.
- **Decode, overstated about 2x.** The -2.9 ms for MXFP8 linears compares cold standalone MXFP8 against a family-wide in-step BF16 estimate. Against the BF16 standalone rows at the same shapes it is -1.3 ms; the KDA o_proj is slower in MXFP8; and shared-expert savings may be hidden by Rubin's side-stream overlap. The -1.5..-2.6 ms MoE figure transfers an EP16 delta that is mostly the DeepGEMM-to-Rubin kernel switch; the quant-only effect at EP32 is about -0.6 ms. Corrected D3-32 r8: 17.0-20.1 ms, 1.23-1.45K tok/s/GPU, not 1.49-1.60K.
- **Prefill, slightly conservative.** The -219 ms holds up, but the like-for-like range is -219..-265 ms, giving 19.4-20.5K tok/s/GPU.

Transfer of mxfp4 derates is handled correctly in principle. Three things change kernel under nvfp4: KDA projections, shared experts (both BF16 to MXFP8), and decode MoE (DeepGEMM fp8_fp4 to NVFP4 at EP32). Prefill MoE keeps the same Rubin nvfp4 kernel and layout as the measured release arm.

What the ledger misses or leaves unverified:
- **B1b's "no kernel change" claim.** It rests on input_scale = 1.0 from a summary file, not the checkpoint. w2 input scales in ModelOpt are typically calibrated and non-pow2, which the pow2 rule in Rubin's norm constants would reject. Verify against the real safetensors before scoping.
- **Real-weight correctness gate.** There is no real-checkpoint load or gsm8k step.
- **Expert tensor names.** The ModelOpt names are unverified.
- **Memory.** Weight memory drops about 33 GiB/GPU at P3-16 and about 15 GiB at D3-32. That eases P3-16 bench feasibility, but D3 r stays capped at 32 by SP_MAX_ROWS.
- **Larger gaps elsewhere.** The checkpoint-independent gap items (sparse MLA, KDA core, shared side stream, BF16 SP GEMMs, top-k merge) are larger than several of the nvfp4 items and should sit in the same plan.
- **FlashInfer citations.** They point at a commit that is not checked out in the local clone (HEAD is f296f9aea).

Proposed fixes respect the placement and precision rules: kernels under kimi_k3, wiring only in model.py, raise rather than fall back, no BF16 upconvert. One caution: B4's minimal step of calling the stock quant_method.apply inside the sdec block must stay graph-safe and is a perf stopgap only.
